title: the-shake-hands-postprocess-the-stamps

intention: The shake is band-outer and hands every postprocess sieve the stamps of all subjects so far, so the cheapest-path compare the bands were built for runs INSIDE the nest as a postprocess sieve — in route (cheapest, prefers) and in the inspector (the teeth sieve reading component_color's stamp) — with every record finding and every route pick byte-identical to today.

(2) inspector: unchanged except green_seal_names_a_tooth reads the component_color stamp from the gradation instead of walking validations itself, so phase_of derives it postprocess. (4) import_sieve.phase_of: a sieve whose signature carries the stamps argument derives 2, one that takes the subject set derives 0 — measured from source, never authored. (5) proofs: nest tooth (band order and stamps handed), route pick byte-identity tooth over test_route.py's fixtures, inspector findings byte-identity by re-sealing its proofs unchanged, phase_of tooth; all under netns.

decisions.text: The preprocess contract is built with a fixture sieve in the nest proof only; the first live preprocess tenant is the probe-nest follow-on ticket.

The loop, literally: shake(assembled, subjects, fire) keeps its signature; inside, gradation = {s: {} for s in subjects} and skipped = set() are owned by shake itself (nothing outside initialises or reads them mid-shake). for band, names in assembled: (band 0) for name in names: keep = set(fire(name, subjects)); for s in subjects: if s in keep: gradation[s][name] = 1.0 else: gradation[s][name] = 1.0; gradation[s]['skipped_by'] = name; skipped.add(s) — a preprocess sieve returns the subject KEYS to score and never a finding; (band 1) for name in names: for s, subject in subjects.items(): if s in skipped: continue; caught = fire(name, subject); findings += caught; gradation[s][name] = 0.0 if caught else 1.0; (band 2) for name in names: for s, subject in subjects.items(): if s in skipped: continue; caught = fire(name, subject, gradation); same scoring. 'assembled' stays exactly what nest() returns today: [(band, [names]), ...] sorted by band. roll_up unchanged: min over the numeric stamps (the 'skipped_by' string is not a score — roll_up reads only float values). The tenant's fire is variadic: fire(name, *args) -> SIEVES[name](*args, ...) — shake picks the arity by band, the tenant passes it through.

Sieve return convention (measured route.py:170-195): a sieve returns a list of findings; [] means the subject passes (stamp 1.0), non-empty means caught (stamp 0.0). cheapest(view, stamps) and prefers(view, stamps) follow it. Both compute the SAME compare over stamps: S = {k for k, row in stamps.items() if all(v == 1.0 for v in row.values() if isinstance(v, float))} (the record-band survivors — every stamp so far is 1.0); P = {k in S whose view['prefers'] names its model}; T = P if P else S. prefers(view, stamps) returns [] iff view's key is in T or not in S, else one finding 'not preferred while a preferred rung survives'. cheapest(view, stamps) returns [] iff view's key is not in S, or view's key is in T and its cash_per_mtoken == min cash over T; else one finding 'not the cheapest survivor'. So roll_up 1.0 after the shake is exactly the pick set: min cash within the preferred tier when any preferred rung survives, else min cash overall — the same host today's sort at :264 + reorder at :272 puts first. For the sieves to see their own key and the domain, each subject view gains 'key' (its subjects-dict key) and 'prefers' (the domain row's prefers list, [] when domain is None); route() resolves the domain row BEFORE the shake (the RouteRefused for an unknown domain moves ahead of the shake, same message). 'preferred' means exactly today's route.py:272: the model name is in the domain row's prefers list.

phase_of detection, literally (cairn/tools/import_sieve/sieve.py:85-99): POSTPROCESS_PARAMS stays {'stamps','scores','gradation','prior_stamps'}; a new PREPROCESS_PARAMS = frozenset({'subjects'}) is added; _local_phase: params & POSTPROCESS_PARAMS -> 2; params & PREPROCESS_PARAMS -> 0; params non-empty -> 1; no params -> 0 (today's rule, kept). Names only, never annotations — a parameter NAME is what the source reads. Proof tooth in cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py beside test_phase_classifies_by_what_the_sieve_reads: def pre(subjects): -> 0, def rec(row, comp_dir): -> 1, def post(row, comp_dir, stamps): -> 2.

When stamps is handed (inside a shake), the sieve reads stamps[row['dir']]['component_color'] before it walks — a KeyError there is the loud, correct failure: the record band did not stamp this component first, so the band order is broken (Law 7, never caught). The read gates nothing and changes no finding byte: the walk over validations and the _finding shape stay exactly inspector.py:3476-3501. phase_of derives 2 from the parameter name (D4), so the live inspector assembly reads postprocess >= 1 from this sieve alone.

The pin tooth is the FIRST act of the build, before route.py changes: a new proof file cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route/proofs/test_the_pick_is_pinned.py with one tooth per fixture in test_route.py that routes today — (load_stacks + _FIXTURE_OVERLAY, generate/qwen2.5:7b) -> 'hex'; (load_stacks + _FIXTURE_OVERLAY, embed/nomic-embed-text) -> 'hex'; (_preference_fixture(['m-dear']), no domain) -> ('p-cheap','m-cheap'); (_preference_fixture(['m-dear']), domain='particular') -> ('p-dear','m-dear'); (_preference_fixture([]), domain='general') -> ('p-cheap','m-cheap') — each asserting route()['survivors'][0] as a literal (provider, model).
